user_report: Terrestrial Auto Focus reported success (best_position=15710) but the focuser ended up visibly out of focus.
optical_setup: Main optical train, ATR585M camera, OnStep focuser (LX200 OnStep), terrestrial scene

cases.name: terrestrial_curve_never_turns_over_before_search_boundary
cases.rationale: Independently derived by inspecting the recorded (position, value) sequence in provenance/incident.json, not by running the implementation: the metric rises monotonically from 7.66 at the start position (14960) all the way to 22.44/22.33 at the search boundary (15960 = start+1000, the configured envelope edge), with no sample anywhere showing a confirmed decline from the running best. A curve that never demonstrably turns over before hitting its own hard search boundary cannot be trusted as a genuine optimum -- by definition the correct report is BEST_AT_SEARCH_LIMIT, never SUCCESS. This case does not fit tests/regressions/_loader.py's generic frame-pair 'BOUNDARIES' driver (this is a decision-algorithm regression over a recorded scalar curve, not an image-analysis regression -- no per-position frames were preserved by the original capture). It is exercised instead by the bespoke tests/regressions/test_issue_35_autofocus_search_regression.py, which replays this exact recorded sequence through BoundedFocusSearcher via a scripted fake focuser/measurer and asserts the fixed status above.
